topics.label: Course introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the lecturer, the course framework, and the learning objectives concerning cancer causation.

topics.label: Genetic, evolutionary, and endogenous origins of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the fundamental view of cancer as a microenvironmental evolutionary process driven by endogenous mutations and inherited predispositions.

topics.label: Environmental carcinogen exposure and epidemiological risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics survey environmental exposures, public perceptions of random versus preventable cancer risk, and geographical epidemiological variations.

topics.label: Oncogenic pathogens and infectious drivers of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious agents promote oncogenesis, using Burkitt lymphoma as a primary case study of multifactorial viral carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Mechanisms of chemical, physical, and xenobiotic mutagenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the biochemical mechanisms through which physical radiation and metabolically activated chemical carcinogens induce DNA damage.

topics.label: Tumor initiation, promotion, and host cell susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the multi-stage model of initiation and promotion and explore how developmental stage and host tissues affect susceptibility to malignant transformation.

topics.label: Methodologies for assessing carcinogenicity and mutational signatures
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental strategies used to determine whether agents are carcinogenic.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and everyday risk-benefit balance
topics.groupedBecause: This closing subtopic summarises the key lecture themes and concludes with reflections on balancing carcinogenic risk against practical benefits in daily life.
